The Art of Trader Joe’s on Instagram: "Swipe to see how Trader Joe’s artists transformed an endcap display for #cincodemayo! 🇲🇽🎉 Take a close look and you might see a secret “5” and “Mayo” encoded in the stacked cans. 👀🙌

In late April, this display featured separate stacked columns of beans, chiles, and taco shells. A few days later, Trader Joe’s crew members rearranged the display, intermixing cans of Black Beans and Green Chiles. To celebrate Cinco de Mayo, they encoded a “5” in the upper portion of the display and the word “Mayo” in the lower portion. The crew brilliantly takes advantage of the color contrast between the cans, embedding a covert message for those who take the time to notice it. 

Stacking is an art form at Trader Joe’s. If you look closely enough, you might be surprised at the secret messages you discover on the shelves! As with many of my favorite artworks at Trader Joe’s, stacked installations are ephemeral—they can appear and disappear in a matter of days. 

Shoutout to the 2023 crew in the Millburn NJ store for this display!

#art #stacking #grocery #cincodemayo #holiday #creative"

title: Puppets - 3 ways!
description: This activity is inspired by Milwaukee artist Anwar Flyod Pruitt that we lost in September of this year. Anwar was a Bubbler collaborator, an artist, and a wonderful human. His work explored paper, particularly cardboard, joy and self expression. Puppets can be incredible tools for storytelling, and I love finding a new way to make one that is innovative and playful. We’ll look at a couple of different types you can make with very simple materials, but all construct and Anwar puppet that uses the physical properties of cardboard and a rubber band to work.
required_materials: cardboard you can cut into squares - should be corrugated
